42017.subject: Biology
42017.question_text: Thick succulent stems and leaves are an adaptation for conservation of water
42017.explanation: Plants living in hot, arid conditions (like deserts) face extreme temperatures and intense sunlight. By storing large amounts of water in their thick succulent stems and fleshy leaves, they can maintain a stable internal temperature. The stored water acts as a thermal buffer, regulating heat and preventing cellular damage or "heat stroke" (desiccation/overheating) when environmental temperatures spike.
